html:
Trajan's Dacian Wars were two wars, in 101 to 102 and 105 to 106, in which the Roman emperor Trajan conquered the kingdom of Dacia north of the Danube, in today's Romania.

The Dacian king Decebalus had forced Rome to pay him under Domitian. Trajan crossed the Danube on a great stone bridge built by Apollodorus of Damascus, took the capital Sarmizegetusa and drove Decebalus to suicide in 106. Dacia's gold mines enriched Rome, and the victory is shown on Trajan's Column in Rome. Settlers came from across the empire. Rome left Dacia around 271, but Romanians see the conquest as the start of their Latin language and people, the meeting of Dacians and Romans.
sum: Trajan's Dacian Wars were two wars, in 101 to 102 and 105 to 106, in which the Roman emperor Trajan conquered the kingdom of Dacia north of the Danube, in today's Romania.
